summary: Manually audited the empirical/anatomical/developmental/prevalence claims in the opening 'What minor lines are' and 'Why some hands don't have them' sections of src/content/lessons/advanced/01-minor-lines-overview.mdx, including claims the audit:claim-risk heuristic does not flag (it pattern-matches prevalence vocabulary, not anatomical/developmental assertions). Narrowed the fetal-development claim from all four major lines to just the heart, head, and life lines -- the three principal palmar flexion creases the repo's own Kimura & Kitagawa (1986) evidence (already cited via blog/beginner/can-palm-lines-change.md) supports as forming before fetal hand movement -- moving the fate line into the 'less fixed' grouping with the minor lines with no anatomical-origin claim asserted about it. Removed the unsupported 'individual constitution, habitual patterns of movement' causal claim for minor lines. Removed the ungrounded 'a clear heart line appears on virtually every adult hand' prevalence/legibility statistic as a redundant restatement of the now evidence-grounded principal-crease claim. Reworded the unsupported 'well within the normal range of human hands' statistical framing to the site's own hand-variation editorial framing. Reworded the unsupported claim that habitual movement and aging 'produce' specific palm markings to state that such surface markings can appear without being an interpretive minor line, dropping the unverified causal mechanism while keeping the practical reading guidance. No new palmistry meaning, combination reading, prevalence estimate, medical/scientific claim, or vague anonymous attribution was introduced to fill any removed wording.

claim_inventory.scope_covered: Opening through the start of 'The four lines in this module' (the 'What minor lines are' and 'Why some hands don't have them -- and what that means' sections), plus a manual re-check of 'How to read minor lines without overweighting them' for any empirical claim (none found there).

dispositions.claim: "The major lines -- the heart line, head line, life line, and fate line -- are anchored in the anatomy of how the hand folds and flexes during fetal development."
dispositions.reasoning: Repository evidence (Kimura & Kitagawa 1986, cited via blog/beginner/can-palm-lines-change.md and docs/source-verification-log.md Pass 1) supports only the three principal palmar flexion creases (heart, head, life) forming in utero before spontaneous fetal hand movement. No repository evidence extends this to the fate line, which can-palm-lines-change.md instead treats as the single most changeable major line with no anatomical-origin claim. Narrowed to the three principal creases; the fate line was moved into the 'less fixed' half of the sentence alongside the minor lines, with no anatomical-origin claim asserted about it either way.

dispositions.claim: "The minor lines are more variable: more influenced by individual constitution, habitual patterns of movement, and ... the specific character and life experience of the person whose hand you're reading."
dispositions.reasoning: No repository evidence supports 'individual constitution' or 'habitual patterns of movement' as an anatomical mechanism producing or shaping minor lines. can-palm-lines-change.md frames comparable language as a traditional/interpretive reading ('often interpreted as reflecting...'), not a physical cause, and 'constitution' elsewhere in the verification log is an interpretive term for what a present line is read to mean, not a claim about what causes a crease to form. Reworded to state only that minor-line presence/clarity varies far more person to person, retaining the already-correctly-hedged 'in the tradition's interpretive terms' framing for the character/life-experience reading.

dispositions.claim: "A clear heart line appears on virtually every adult hand."
dispositions.reasoning: No repository evidence supports a specific prevalence rate ('virtually every') or legibility rate ('clear') for the heart line; the site's established practice (Pass 1's simian-line prevalence correction) is caution around bare prevalence figures. The comparative point this sentence made is already covered, without an ungrounded statistic, by the corrected line-21 claim that the three principal creases appear on essentially every hand as a matter of fetal-development anatomy. Removed as redundant and less well-grounded than the earlier sentence.

dispositions.claim: "Both are well within the normal range of human hands."
dispositions.reasoning: No repository evidence establishes a statistical 'normal range' for minor-line density. The surrounding paragraph is the site's own editorial framing (hand variation is not a deficiency), not an external prevalence claim. Reworded to 'Both are simply how hands vary -- neither is a more complete or more correct hand than the other,' preserving the point without borrowing unsupported statistical language.

dispositions.claim: "Surface texture, skin creasing from habitual movement, and the natural aging of the palm all produce lines that are anatomical rather than interpretive."
dispositions.reasoning: No repository evidence supports habitual movement or aging as a mechanism that produces new palm lines in adulthood; the repo's only embryological evidence (Kimura & Kitagawa) covers prenatal crease/ridge formation, not adult line formation. The instructional point (some visible marks are not meaningful minor lines) does not require asserting an unverified specific cause. Reworded to state that such surface markings 'can appear on a palm without being a minor line in the interpretive sense,' dropping the causal claim while keeping the practical guidance.

Procedural/methodological guidance for telling a true minor line from surface noise, not an empirical or attributed claim; consistent with the parallel guidance already published in advanced/02-marriage-relationship-lines.mdx. This pass reworded the surrounding sentence's causal-mechanism wording but left this hedge's own sentence untouched.

dispositions.claim: "most" -- "the features that carry the most interpretive weight"
dispositions.reasoning: The site's own curriculum-weighting statement, not an external prevalence/consensus claim. Outside this task's scoped opening/general-method passages and not touched.

source_preflight.notes: All prevalence/frequency wording in the touched passages ('virtually every', 'normal range') was removed or reworded to what repository evidence supports. The one retained scientific/anatomical assertion (principal-crease formation before fetal hand movement) is traced to Kimura & Kitagawa (1986) via existing repository citations; no scientific/anatomical claim was retained or introduced without that grounding. No combination reading was invented -- the corrections narrow or remove claims rather than adding new interpretive content. No vague anonymous authority ('modern palmists', 'some writers', etc.) was introduced. No quotation marks appear in the edited sentences, so no quotation-fidelity check applied beyond confirming none were added. No medical, legal, financial, deterministic-relationship, or predictive-science claim was introduced or retained.
